name: Saturn
tagline: The ringed giant — its halo of ice spans 280,000 km yet is meters thin.
history: Galileo saw Saturn's rings in 1610 but could not resolve them — he called them 'ears'; Huygens identified the ring system in 1655, and Cassini found the division that bears his name. The rings are countless particles of nearly pure water ice, likely the remains of a shattered moon or captured comet, and may be geologically young. The Cassini orbiter spent thirteen years in the Saturn system (2004–2017), discovering geysers on Enceladus that vent a subsurface ocean into space and dropping the Huygens probe onto Titan — the only landing ever made in the outer Solar System.
